title: Task
description: Atomic unit of work produced by the Planner from features/stories. Source file: governance/tasks.json ({"entries": [Task]}). Lifecycle constraint checked by self-check: at most `parallel` entries of the active sprint in_progress (D-0084) -- and never entries from two different ratified sprints at once. A task in no ratified sprint is still one at a time.

title.description: A sentence naming the state that will be true when the work is done, not a noun phrase and not an id. Real examples: "The close is not blocked by bytecode" (T-0217); "The graph does not crash on a repo it has never seen" (T-0213); "Rulings whose machinery was deleted are retired" (D-0081). A title like "fix session-check" names a file and a verb, so a cold session cannot tell what was wrong or how anyone would know it stopped being wrong.

acceptance_check.description: Stated before work starts. The task is done when this passes, not when the output looks done. It is command-verifiable: it names what must be observably true AND the suite that shows it. Real examples: "graph gov build succeeds on a GOV_ROOT whose governance directory does not exist yet, and tests/graph-cli-tests.sh exits 0" (T-0213); "A tree containing __pycache__ or .pyc files closes session-check exit 0 when everything else traces to a worked task, an unauthorised source file still FAILs by name, and tests/session-check-tests.sh exits 0" (T-0217). "works" and "tests pass" are not checks: neither names what would have to be false for it to fail.

issue.description: The issue this task was promoted from (task new --issue, D-S041, SX-036). task accept TELLs it and session check WARNs while an accepted task's issue stays open; resolving the issue stays a person's act. Absent when the task was not created from an issue.

task_order.description: Required before the task can enter a sprint (D-0005). The task's story field holds the one user story (required unless the sprint is hotfix).

light.description: The light lane (D-0072 boundary 4, D-0073): an order minted from User's message in a standalone session rather than prepackaged by the app. Absent or false means the full lane. task-lint demotes its story and context-files FAILs to TELL when this is true; the acceptance-check and single-verification-command FAILs hold in BOTH lanes.

scope.description: What this task changes: the change, the site it lands at, and the evidence it rests on, so the implementer searches for none of the three. Real example: "Add build and OS artefacts to session-check's scope exemption at :202, alongside governance/*, *.MD and .claude/*. Reproduced in canon acceptance run 4 - the close FAILed on agents/__pycache__/*.pyc" (T-0217).

out_of_scope.description: Explicit do-NOT-touch list — the scope-creep brake. Each entry names the thing AND why it is out, so a later reader can tell a deliberate exclusion from an oversight. Real examples: "Any other exemption. Only build and OS artefacts - a file an agent wrote is still a file an order must own" (T-0217); "I-0112's read-side self-heal on staleness - a NEW capability, frozen out; the issue stays documented" (T-0213).

verification_command.description: The command that proves the acceptance check passes. Exactly ONE runnable command, stating how to run it: "sh tests/session-check-tests.sh" (T-0217), not "tests/session-check-tests.sh" - 27 of 38 suites are mode 644 and exit 126 when invoked bare (D-0041). A composite command belongs in a script this points at.

fails_when.description: Optional (SX-003, D-S016): the broken state the verification command must catch -- what has to be true for the check to go red. Guidance and evidence only: task lint echoes it, task brief prints it, scrumux-app shows it at acceptance (and says when none was declared). Nothing refuses an order without it.

context.description: Full procedural context pack — assembled, not searched.

why.description: What the implementer is meant to look FOR in that file, never what the file is. Real examples: ".claude/scripts/session-check | :202, the exemption case"; "agents/lib/governance_graph.py | the writer I-0111 traces to"; "tests/graph-cli-tests.sh | gains its own GOV_ROOT so it stops racing the live indexes". A why that restates the filename tells the reader nothing they did not already have.

refs.description: Governance records that bear on the task.

commands.description: Ground-truth commands to run (tests, health checks).

expected_artifacts.description: Paths this task will CREATE. Optional by necessity (I-0064): an order can name the files an implementer must read, but not files that do not exist yet. NOT in required — a sixth required key would invalidate every order already written.

receipt.description: The last task-verify run, written by the script and never by hand (T-0187). Overwritten on every run — the last receipt wins, because acceptance asks whether the CURRENT state is verified. Green = rc 0 AND checks_failed 0; scrumux task accept refuses anything else, and refuses a task with no receipt at all (D-0072 boundary 5).

at_epoch.description: When the receipt was written, in epoch seconds. The close compares this against the mtime of every file the order covers, which is how verified-then-kept-typing is caught; date alone is a day and cannot resolve it. Optional: receipts written before this field existed cannot be judged for freshness, and the close says so rather than guessing.

command.description: The task_order.verification_command as it was run. The close compares it against the order's command, which is how a verify run against something easier is caught.

rc.description: Exit code of the verification command itself.

checks_run.description: What ran: the order's own verification command, plus any registered repo-health checks executed alongside it. Always at least 1 on an honest verify — a receipt reporting 0 is a green that proved nothing, and the close fails it.

file_hashes.description: sha256 hex of every covered file (task_order.context.files[].path and expected_artifacts) that existed when this receipt was written, keyed by repo-relative path (SX-024). session check's 'receipt fresh' compares CONTENT with these: a differing hash, or a covered file present now and absent here, is a change. Absent on receipts written before the field; the close then falls back to comparing mtimes with at_epoch.

acceptance.description: User's final-authority ruling on this task (D-0076: acceptance targets the task, not a review record). Write-once while accepted is true; a rejection carries accepted:false and a reason, and the task returns to in_progress.

authority.description: How the act was authorised. direct = a person said so in this session; app = taken through scrumux-app, which is the authority (User's ruling, 2026-08-28), where no dispatch session is involved -- a sprint ratification is opened at repo level and belongs to no session, and naming one would invent it; app:<session> = the same, for an act that DOES belong to a dispatched session; standing:D-XXXX = a ratified delegation, and the D- ref must resolve.

reason.description: Required on a rejection — what has to change before it comes back. Name the defect and the bar: "The receipt is green but its command is not the order's own command - re-verify against the order" beats "not done", which names neither.

reverified.description: the acceptor re-ran the order verification_command at acceptance time rather than reading the receipt (I-0139). Absent on acceptances recorded before that was required.

receipt.description: The receipt this acceptance gated on, copied in and frozen (D-S018, SX-013). A later task verify never rewrites it; its runs go to post_acceptance_checks. Absent on acceptances recorded before the field, whose live `receipt` is then the frozen one.

check_fingerprint.description: A fingerprint of the check that was accepted (D-S045, SX-041): sha256 of each file or directory the verification command references that existed in the repo at acceptance (a script, a test path; a directory hashes its sorted regular files). scrumux-app compares it with the files now and shows 'the check itself changed since acceptance' beside post-acceptance runs. files may be empty (the command names no file); absent on acceptances recorded before the field, which reads as unknown.

superseded.description: Why this task was retired, and optionally the task that replaces it (T-0115/I-0059).

post_acceptance_checks.description: task verify runs made AFTER acceptance (D-S018, SX-013), newest last, the last 10 kept. The acceptance receipt is not changed by them. A red newest entry is drift -- surfaced by session check (WARN) and scrumux-app -- not a broken task.

receipt_history.description: task verify runs made BEFORE acceptance (SX-034), newest last, the last 10 kept; the newest is the run `receipt` records. A red run followed by a green one stays visible here, so review can see what the last receipt alone hides (a failed check that left side effects, then a green rerun). Never gates acceptance. Absent on tasks verified before the field: no history recorded.

blocked.description: Why the task is blocked, from `task status T-XXXX blocked --reason TEXT` (SX-006): a step only the operator can take (a deploy), a permission a session cannot grant itself. Present only while status is blocked; any other status change removes it. scrumux-app shows it and offers the operator's way through.
